description: Figure 13 is a weak-beam dark-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–28% Al, comprising one large main frame plus two unlabelled magnified insets (top-left and top-right). The main frame shows thin, bright, mostly straight dislocation lines and segments on a dark, slightly mottled background; many of the straight segments and their junctions are labelled with the letter "r". A solid white arrow in the lower-right corner indicates the direction of the imaging g vector, and a printed black scale bar in the bottom-right corner reads 0.2 µm. The two insets show the r-marked reaction configurations at higher magnification, resolving intersecting line segments that meet at sharp, extended junctions/cusps. The caption states the zone axis is near [001], the imaging g vector (arrowed) is 2 0 0, and the imaging condition is near g:3–4g. Beyond the 0.2 µm scale bar and the "r" labels, no numeric values are printed on the image. The figure, together with the citing text, demonstrates that the straight parallel dislocations marked r are reaction products — locks formed by two different 1/2⟨111⟩ superdislocations — rather than ordinary glide dislocations.
measured_quantities: spatial length scale (µm), from the 0.2 µm scale bar

observations.observation: The figure is a single weak-beam (dark-field) TEM micrograph with two magnified insets at top-left and top-right; bright dislocation lines appear on a dark background.
A printed scale bar in the bottom-right corner reads 0.2 µm.
A solid white arrow in the lower-right region marks the direction of the imaging g vector; its magnitude (2 0 0) is not printed on the image, only stated in the caption.
The label 'r' is printed at many separate locations in the main frame and in both insets, marking the reaction dislocation segments.
Numerous dislocations in the main frame are long, straight and roughly parallel, consistent with near-screw orientations; others form irregular curved networks.
The caption states the imaged material is deformed Fe–28% Al.
The caption states the zone axis is near [001], the imaging g vector (arrowed) is 2 0 0, and the imaging condition is near g:3–4g.
The caption states the micrograph shows superdislocation reactions (marked r) and that the insets show the reaction dislocation in more detail.

The citing text states that the r-marked straight dislocations are produced as reactions between segments of glissile ⟨111⟩-type superdislocations with different ⟨111⟩ Burgers vectors lying in different {110} glide planes.
The citing text states that imaging with many different g vectors shows the reaction produces a pair of edge dislocations with ⟨100⟩ Burgers vector sitting in a sessile configuration on a cube plane.
The citing text gives the example reaction [111] + [1 1̄ 1] forming a pair of [100] edge dislocations along the [010] direction, hence lying in a (001) plane.
The citing text states such configurations constitute locks that prevent further room-temperature superdislocation motion.

subfigures.description: Large weak-beam dark-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–28% Al showing bright thin dislocation lines and segments over a dark background. Numerous straight segments and junctions are annotated with the label 'r'. A white arrow at lower right marks the g-vector direction; a printed scale bar reads 0.2 µm.
Magnified inset of a reaction configuration: several dislocation segments meeting at a sharp junction, with one segment labelled 'r' twice. Shows the reaction node in more detail than the main frame.
Magnified inset of another reaction configuration with intersecting dislocation segments labelled 'r', showing the extended junction morphology rejected in the main micrograph.
